title: Balanced split bound on the squared larger part
statement:
Let $m, n \in \bbn$ satisfy $3m \le 2n$ and $3(n - m) \le 2n$, so that neither of the two parts $m$ and $n - m$ exceeds two-thirds of $n$. Then
\[
9 \cdot \max\bigl(m^2,\,(n - m)^2\bigr) \le 4 n^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: 3m ≤ 2n (first part at most two-thirds of n)
3(n − m) ≤ 2n (second part at most two-thirds of n)
replaced:
Let $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $3m \le 2n$ and $3(n - m) \le 2n$.
Then $9 \cdot \max(m^2,\,(n-m)^2) \le 4n^2$.
This arithmetic inequality captures the key quantitative gain obtained when a split is
\emph{balanced}: neither piece exceeds $\tfrac{2}{3}$ of the total.
